subject: Security exhibit access limits and pen-test scheduling
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@nexushealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nexushealth.com
Date: 2026-08-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Security exhibit & pen test: scope / access

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the welcome call last week. Procurement and our InfoSec team have reviewed the MSA + proposed security exhibit and we need a bit more detail before we can sign. A few items to clarify:

- SOC 2: we require the latest Type II report and a summary of the in-scope systems and any carve-outs.
- Pen test language: we cannot accept open prod access. We need confirmation that testing will be limited to a staging environment or a copy of production with sanitized data.
- Audit access: we prefer a clearly timeboxed, limited-inspection clause rather than open inspection rights. For annual audits we'd like a 2-week notice window and an agreed evidence cadence (monthly artifacts + quarterly summaries).
- Evidence: sample set we expect includes network diagrams, change-control logs, and audit logs for the last 90 days.

Attached is our standard security questionnaire (partial) with the redlines our legal team proposed. Can you confirm Redwood's stance and proposed rewrites? Also please propose 2-3 pen-test windows in September/October if staging access is possible.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Senior Security Manager, Nexus Health
[Attachment: nexus_questionnaire_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@nexushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-20T13:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit & pen test: scope / access

Hi Samantha — thanks, very helpful detail. Looping in Legal and Product to propose concrete contract language so we can close this quickly. High level: we can meet Nexus's requirements if we agree the following tradeoffs.

1) SOC 2: we will provide the most recent Type II report and a one-page scope mapping for the security exhibit. We will not disclose raw audit evidence but can provide summarized artifacts and attestation language.

2) Pen test: Redwood cannot grant unfettered prod access. We will provide a staging environment (production-equivalent with sanitized PII) for penetration testing. That environment will be read/write for test traffic and will be timeboxed. Tests against production are only allowed via a signed exception with a 30-day notice and dedicated Redwood on-call support. We will require a rules-of-engagement doc and a POA/NDA for testers.

3) Audit / inspection: propose a limited-inspection clause with: 14-day notice for standard inspections, evidence delivery cadence of monthly artifact bundles (logs + change-control summary) and quarterly executive summaries. For formal audits that require deeper access, propose a mutually agreed 10-business-day window with specific artifact lists; any hands-on inspection will be carried out in staging unless otherwise negotiated.

I attached a draft redline to the security exhibit and a short Ops checklist for pen tests. If that looks OK, we can send an updated MSA appendix and a DocuSign bundle with two scheduling options for pen testing:
- Option A: Sep 27–29 (three-day window, staging)
- Option B: Oct 18–20 (three-day window, staging)

Can you confirm which option your team prefers and whether the staging approach works?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redlines_v1.docx (docx)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-21T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: proposed language and negotiation plan (Nexus Health)

Marissa / Laura / Priyom — quick internal note before we send formal redlines back to Nexus. My suggested playbook:

- Keep a single paragraph in the MSA security exhibit that limits inspection to "reasonable, timeboxed, and specific" requests and requires a 2-week notice for standard evidence pulls. Don't use the term "unfettered."
- For pen tests: codify staging-only as default. If Nexus insists on production, route to Legal and require: (a) 30-day notice; (b) signed Rules of Engagement; (c) Redwood technical escort; (d) indemnity carveout limited to negligence.
- Evidence cadence: propose monthly bundles containing predefined artifact types (network diagram, change-control summary, last 90 days of system event logs — redacted). Quarterly attestation letters from Redwood with SOC 2 summary should be acceptable.
- Add a short SLA for evidence turnaround (we propose 10 business days for standard artifacts, 20 for ad-hoc deep dives).

I've drafted specific clause language in the attached spreadsheet and called out fallback negotiation points. If Legal wants, we can include an "inspection lite" appendix that enumerates what we will not provide (raw backups, unreleased internal debugging data, full raw logs older than 90 days).

If that aligns, Marissa please send Nexus the revised redline + DocuSign and offer the two test windows. I'll be available for a quick sync before we hit send.

-Karthik
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pen-test-ops.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@nexushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Final: revised exhibit redline and pen-test schedule options

Samantha — thanks for the fast turn. Per internal alignment we've prepared a concise redline that narrows inspection rights and formalizes the pen-test ops. Summary of changes (high level):

- Inspection: limited to reasonable, timeboxed requests with a 14-day standard notice; monthly artifact bundles + quarterly attestation.
- Pen testing: default staging-only testing. Production testing requires a 30-day exception request, Rules of Engagement, Redwood technical escort, and indemnity terms.
- Evidence turnaround: standard artifacts delivered within 10 business days; targeted deep-dive requests 20 business days.

Please find the redline attached and a DocuSign link to execute the updated security exhibit. Once we have executed the redline, we can lock a pen-test window — we currently have Sep 27–29 and Oct 18–20 open for staging-based tests.

If Nexus prefers production testing, let us know immediately and we'll route to Legal for an exception workflow; expect a longer review.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redlines_v1.docx (docx)]
